newsitem.title: UK: Host of potential Clyde counter bidders seen.
newsitem.headline: Host of potential Clyde counter bidders seen.

text.p: Canadian companies, German utilities and a Dutch group are likely contenders to rival Gulf Canada's 432 million stg bid for Clyde Petroleum Plc, oil industry sources said on Wednesday.
"The most likely candidates will either come from Canada, Germany or the Netherlands," one source said.

But even if -- contrary to market expectations -- no white knight appeared, Clyde is likely to lose its independence, as its five major investors are believed to be quite happy with Gulf's 105 pence per share offer.
"I cannot see any circumstances in which this company won't be taken over," another source said.
Industry sources speculate that Clyde's three biggest shareholders, who together own 44.46 percent, bought in over the past three years at an average price of 50 pence per share.
This compares with a current price of 117 pence, which is well above Gulf Canada's offer of 105 pence, reflecting widespread hopes of a counter offer.
Clyde's defence document, issued on Sunday, gives the following list of main shareholders and their stakes:
-- bank Schroders Plc, which holds 19.48 percent
-- investment fund PDFM Ltd, a UBS unit with 14.86 percent
-- Capital Group Companies with 10.12 percent
-- Norwich Union Life Insurance Society with 8.09
-- Wittington Investments Ltd with a stake of 4.83 percent.
Analysts' list of potential contenders, meanwhile, includes Canadian firms such as Pan Canadian and Talisman Energy Inc .
They are widely considered to be keen to expand their North Sea interest by taking out European companies trading at a lower cash flow multiple then themselves.
U.S. independent exploration and production may come to the fore for the same reason, analysts said.
"These (the Canadians and the U.S.) are the usual suspects," said an industry watcher, who declined to be named.
Another source believes there is also a fair chance German utilities and energy groups such as Ruhrgas AG and Wintershall may step into the fray.
These companies might be keen to use Clyde as a vehicle to boost their presence in the Dutch part of the North Sea as oil and gas production at home is dwindling, the source said.
Another industry watcher also mentioned Netherlands-based Oranje Nassau Energy BV, a privately owned firm with overlapping interests in Dutch gas projects, as a potential contender.
